2Getting There

Turkey is easily accessible from South Africa via major carriers like Turkish Airlines and Emirates, flying into Istanbul Airport (IST) or Sabiha Gökçen (SAW). Domestic connections are efficient, linking to Cappadocia, Bodrum, Izmir, and Antalya.

3How to Sell Turkey

1. Escorted Tours

Why sell it:

  • Great value for money, includes accommodation, transport, and select meals
  • Ideal for first-time visitors wanting to cover multiple highlights efficiently

Target market:

Budget-Conscious Travellers Solo Travellers & Small Groups First-Timers to Turkey

2. Tailor-Made Travel

Why sell it:

  • Customisable itineraries with flexible stays
  • Great for couples or families wanting a relaxed pace

Target market:

Repeat Visitors Honeymooners & Families Independent Travellers
Selling TipOffer to pair city stays with coastal relaxation, for example, Istanbul + Cappadocia + Bodrum.

4Istanbul – Where East Meets West

The Golden Horn divides the European side of Istanbul into the Old City and the New City.

Top Attractions

  • Topkapi Palace – home of the Ottoman Sultans
  • Hippodrome – the ancient Roman circus
  • Blue Mosque – iconic and serene
  • Hagia Sophia – the crown jewel of Byzantine architecture
  • Underground Basilica Cistern – a massive underground water cavern of beautiful arches and Roman support columns
  • Grand Bazaar – endless treasures and bargains
  • Galata Tower & Taksim Square – modern Istanbul's heart
  • Istiklal Avenue – shopping at brand stores and riding the old tram

Experiences to Recommend

  • Evening stroll through the Old City
  • Bosphorus Cruise (day or sunset)
  • Street simit (Turkish bagel) with Nutella or cream cheese
  • Shopping for Turkish Delight
  • Ride the nostalgic tram along Istiklal Avenue

Getting Around Istanbul

  • Walk: Ideal in the Old City, major sights are close together
  • Tram: Efficient and inexpensive, tap your card to pay
  • Funicular: Quick connection between the ferry terminal and Istiklal Avenue
  • Taxi: Avoid during peak times due to heavy traffic
  • Ferry: Perfect for sightseeing and hopping between the European & Asian sides

5Beyond Istanbul

Cappadocia – The Land of Fairy Chimneys

  • UNESCO World Heritage Site
  • Famous for hot air balloon rides at sunrise
  • Explore Göreme Open-Air Museum, underground cities, and cave hotels

Pamukkale – The Cotton Castle

  • Known for its white travertine terraces and natural thermal pools
  • Visit the ancient city of Hierapolis nearby

Bodrum – The Aegean Playground

  • Trendy coastal town, great nightlife and beaches
  • Ideal for Gullet (Blue Cruise) departures
  • Mix of history, glamour, and sea views

Kusadasi – Gateway to Ephesus

  • Close to the ancient ruins of Ephesus
  • Ideal for short beach stays or cruise stopovers
  • Great shopping and ferry access to Greek islands

Marmaris – Mediterranean Charm

  • Laid-back vibe with a beautiful marina
  • Known for fresh seafood, local wines, and friendly locals

6Food, Glorious Food!

Must-Try Dishes

  • Pide (Turkish pizza) – baked with cheese, meat, or spinach
  • Kebabs – with grilled tomatoes, onions, and rice
  • Clay Pot Stew (Testi Kebab) – dramatic table-side crack open!
  • Meze Platters – dips like hummus, ezme, and baba ghanoush
  • Baklava – flaky layers with pistachios and syrup
  • Katmer – dessert with pistachio cream in phyllo pastry
  • Turkish Breakfast – olives, cheeses, simit, eggs, jams, and çay (tea)

8Selling Tips for Consultants

Know Your Traveller

  • Couples & Honeymooners: Sell Cappadocia cave hotels, sunset balloon rides, and romantic Bosphorus dinners
  • Families: Suggest Istanbul + Kusadasi + Pamukkale, mixing culture and beaches
  • Adventurous Travellers: Promote hot air ballooning, paragliding in Oludeniz, and Blue Cruises

Upsell Opportunities

  • Private airport transfers
  • Traditional Turkish Bath (Hammam) experiences
  • Cooking classes or food tours
  • Cappadocia sunrise balloon rides (book early!)

Insider Tips

  • Recommend carrying cash, not all small vendors accept cards. Credit cards are accepted in the Grand Bazaar but carry a fee; street vendors will take cash
  • Dress modestly when visiting mosques. A headscarf is free to use at the Blue Mosque, but needs to be hired at Hagia Sophia, packing a personal pashmina saves money. Women must cover their heads
  • Encourage early morning sightseeing to avoid queues and heat. Pre-booking or joining a tour where the guide holds the tickets helps clients skip the queues
  • Suggest downloading Google Translate for menu and sign reading, though English is widely understood

9Why Sell Turkey?

  • Offers excellent value for money and rich cultural diversity
  • Easy visa process for South Africans
  • Diverse experiences: history, food, nature, beaches, and adventure
  • Ideal add-on to Greece or Egypt itineraries
